The architecture

One canvas, grown by bands. Band 1 is the analyze pulse — the only path that writes. Band 2 is everything that reads it. It is a cycle, not a stack: two edges point backwards, because an answer reads what the pulse wrote and analyze is itself just another command. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a block to trace its wiring, double-click or use the i to open its page.

click to highlight · double-click or the i to open · click an edge to trace it · Esc clears 100%

What this band does NOT show

A boundary is not completeness (rules.md §11 — the standard, which lives in the skill). These two bands draw the write path and the read path. They do not show:

  • Each of the 42 commands individually. Band 2 draws the dispatcher, the contract they all implement, and the two places an answer can come from. It does not draw 42 boxes — that would be a folder tree, not a journey.
  • The watcher. An incremental pulse re-enters Band 1 mid-way rather than at the top, and the edge that says so belongs to a band about evolution over time.
  • Federation. Cross-repository linking exists and is reached from conducks link; no band crosses it yet.
  • The five core features these paths cross without stopping at. contracts, utils, algorithms, registry and bootstrap each have a module note instead of a container.

Band 2 crosses three unaudited layers. domain, interfaces and registry have not had the structural pass core got. The PATH drawn here was read file by file; the layers behind it were not swept. Core was declared clean and two dead subsystems were found in it afterwards, so nothing on this band claims those three are cleaner — the n-no block in the answer container says so on the canvas itself.

Read log

Every block on this canvas was written from a file opened during the ADR 0150 core campaign, not from memory — the rule that produced five corrected claims on the repo this standard came from. The derived list below is generated from the anchors themselves.

Band 1 read at d184968 — every block came from a file opened during the ADR 0150 core campaign, whose log docs/deep_clean.md records what was measured at each step and what each measurement cost.

Band 2 read at 45a65be — the dispatcher and its command contract (interfaces/cli), the MCP anchor and vault hold (interfaces/tools/shared), the composition root and its deferred-graph guard (src/registry), the filter builder and the staleness warning. Read for this band specifically, not recalled from the core sweep, because none of those three layers was in it.

A visual is traced at a moment and starts rotting immediately. Anchors are checked by conducks visuals-lint; the layout is computed by ELK and verified by a collision gate that refuses to emit an overlapping picture. Neither reads prose — that an anchor resolves is not evidence the sentence attached to it is still true.
